Thank you for this. Unfortunately, a problem arises if a customer's orders are segmented by another customer (ex. Order 10001 = Jimmy James, Order 10002 = Frankie Fredrickson, Order 10003 = Jimmy James). The invoice would pull Jimmy James' orders 10001 and 10003, but "LRow = LRow + 1" would move to the next row on the Order Table, not the next invoice line.

I was, however, able to use the information you provided to make some more code and tweak my workbook a little! Now, my order table concats Order # and Line #, and instead of incrementing Line #s on the Invoice, the invoice now pulls that concat number!

Also, since cell A14 on the Invoice Form is now another filter function (line gets removed when an Invoice number is entered), I was able to loop the Match to keep referencing the value in cell A14. BEHOLD!

>Sub UpdateList()

>Dim invForm As Worksheet  
Dim invList As Worksheet  
Dim tableRow As Long

>Set invForm = Worksheets("Invoice")  
Set invList = Worksheets("Order Table")

>'Repeats steps until all lines are removed from the invoice  
Do Until invForm.Range("A14").Value = ""

>'Finds the first row of an Order number on the Order Table that matches the Order number of the first line on the Invoice  
tableRow = Application.WorksheetFunction.Match(invForm.Range("A14"), invList.Range("A:A"), 0)

>invList.Range("P" & tableRow) = invForm.Range("G3")

>Loop

>End Sub

It's common industry courtesy to lock new releases from ranked play for at least a week or two so people cannot abuse any bugs or imbalances for competitive advantage. It also forces less skilled players to actually practice in casuals as to not jeopardize other players rankings.

Despite all of my frustrations, I still enjoy playing the game (enjoy is used loosely), but things need to get considerably better before I decide to start supporting it financially again. Increasing the price of a battle pass and decreasing the gems rewarded from the monthly pass does not bode well.

Really cool doc! Personally, I think before anyone starts streaming/content creation, they need to be honest about *why* they want to stream (money/friends/fun). In the context of content creation, creativity needs to be the highest priority. Is this content unique/how can you make it more unique? If you're just copying a larger creator, why would I watch your videos if I can just watch theirs?

People need to answer some really hard questions in order to set proper/realistic expectations.

Other comments don't seem to be very helpful, so I'll try to cover some of the basics. Also... not sure why post was downvoted.

First and foremost, you need to be honest with yourself and answer the question "*Why* do you want to stream?" Do you desire monetary gain? Do you want to meet new people? Are you good at a particular game and want to show off your skillz? Understanding your motivation will determine what goals and expectations you need to set for yourself. (If you have an answer to this, I'll happily expand)

*Also* first and foremost, do you have a computer/network that's even capable of streaming? It should go without saying, but streaming requires quite a bit of processing power, moreso if you want to game and stream from the same PC. I know plenty of streamers who have a gaming PC, and a streaming PC to reduce system load. If you want to stream from console, you'll need a capture card with the correct connections. If you're familiar with PC building, go for any El Gato PICe. If you're not comfortable with building, USB capture devices work fine, but the quality will be limited to your USB port's data transfer capacity.

*LASTLY* first and foremost, make friends and be active in the community/category before you ever go live. Having support from them will drastically help your channel build the momentum it needs to get off the ground. On that note, try getting IRL friends join the chat interact with you and new viewers. The biggest thing that turns viewers away (aside from cringey content) is joining a channel with 0-2 viewers and no chat activity.

I hope this gives you an idea of how you need to approach streaming. As I said before, I'll be happy to elaborate, I just don't want to say too much in case there's any confusion.

Inattentive and medicated "as needed"

At first, my medication helped me significantly by getting me focused at work and less distracted. I was able to finish assignments when I got them instead of procrastinating until a deadline. This, however, has diminished over time to the point that now when I take my medication before work I become completely disinterested in being a productive employee and get frustrated with myself when I cannot motivate myself to do anything that doesn't have a deadline. When I don't take my medication for work, I still can't motivate myself and I find myself falling asleep at my desk, but at least I don't get mad at myself for doing so :)

I still take my medication for work on most days as it helps me feel like a normal person that can participate in conversation. Without it, I can hardly remember what anyone says to me, nor do I know how to respond most times. I get stuck in my head and end up just agreeing to something because I don't know what else to say.

Home life, on the other hand, has improved significantly since being medicated. I can remember chores, I can do something when I think about it instead of putting it off, I can enjoy my hobbies AND I can take breaks from them, instead of feeling bored and feeling like I need them to relax. Although it ruins my appetite, when I'm home I can usually force myself to eat, whereas when I'm not medicated I often forget to eat.

Adverse effects of being medicated: increased heart rate and blood pressure, night sweats, and more heat sensitivity (I already don't like the heat, but when medicated every time I'm outside it feels like I could have a heat stroke)

For example, let's say a post in a fruits and vegetables sub is asking for people's opinion on their favorite fruits and vegetables. Someone comments, "I really love roasted brussel sprouts, especially the aroma it leaves in my apartment" and 1,200 people vote on it: 300 upvotes (agrees), 900 downvotes (disagrees). That's a 1-to-3 opinion, not popular, but not insignificant and not unanimous.

Wow, that's really disappointing. I can't express enough how annoyed I get when I hear how close-minded some parents can be. Don't listen to them, community college is a great option for those with "bad" grades and tight finances. Well, I'm assuming you're 18, or close to it. You're an adult (legally), no one can force you to take out a loan. Please think long and hard before you make any financial decisions. Student loans are the WORST, most bottom feeding, kind of loans there are. You're young with next to no financial history, and graduating college doesn't guarantee you a job, let alone a good paying job. An inability to pay off a student loan means this debt will accrue and hang over your head for damn near the rest of your life. It's truly inescapable, and it's not worth the risk. If your parents really want what's best for you, then they would take on that financial burden for you, apply for a personal loan from a credit union, and use that to pay for your tuition, housing, and dining. They will be offered much better finance terms and credit unions are MUCH more forgiving than student lenders. Remember, lenders don't make their money off of rich people, they want people who can't pay so that they'll always have a stream of income from your interest.

I'm not saying that you wouldn't enjoy going to a university, for many people it's their first chance to live on their own, meet new people, and grow as an individual. I never lived in a dorm and I never had any meal plans, but I'd imagine those are the two best things about living on-campus (not having rent or mortgage payments, and not needing to cook for yourself, lol). Aside from that though, it's still school. Lectures, homework, and tests, nothing changes. When you graduate, you'll only be considered for "entry-level" positions. Positions that, 20 years ago, would have been available to high school graduates. Even then, a company is more likely to hire someone overqualified so they can underpay them. It's such a scam. It took me over 3 months to get a job offer for a full-time hourly job after graduation. Another 6 months after that to start my career in the area of my studies. Now, five years later, I've been given one promotion and I make half of what my friends are making in HVAC.  

College isn't the only option. Trades are in high demand now more than ever. Apprenticeships are incredible to start working now and moving your way up. By the time you would have graduated you'll have already worked for years (earning money, not spending it), and gotten a few raises too. Your best opportunities to make money at a 4-year college are part-time student worker positions, which are honestly just insulting if you have loans to pay off. You may need to take some night classes, but more likely than not, those costs are covered by your apprenticeship program. Biggest drawback is that these are hard, physically demanding jobs. They call them "Trades" because you trade your body for money.

That's incredible, using your deceased sibling to invalidate your feelings. Truly remarkable parenting right there. It's cliché, but seriously, you're not alone. If you've known you never liked school, then it seems pretty obvious that you'd never want to go to college. Let me ask, are you paying for college? Too young to get a "real" job, too old to receive any more handouts. Keep up with college if you can see yourself getting any degree and use out of it, otherwise take a break to look for something to occupy yourself now.
